title: {Syn} Miller-Rabin Is the Practical Prime Filter
content:
The Miller-Rabin test is a probabilistic primality test that quickly rejects most composites. Repeating it with independent bases drives the error probability down extremely fast.

For bounded machine integers, carefully chosen deterministic base sets are known, which makes the same idea both fast and exact in many programming contexts.

Why it matters: algorithms keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
